regions.region: Scheme 2 and its ligand/result rows, center right
regions.finding: Two actual ligand-specific experiments are shown. The (S,S)-Ph-Box row is the same experiment as Table 1 entry 1 and was merged into that record; the (R,R)-Ph-Box row is a separate reported experiment.

Describes stage-1 amination, solvent removal, THF addition, Pd/PPh3/K2CO3 treatment, cyclization, chromatographic separability, and ligand-dependent configurations; associated with the Scheme 2/Table 1 records rather than counted again.
Citations and background literature, not experiments newly reported by this paper.

regions.region: Table 1 reaction diagram, rows 1-9, and footnotes
regions.finding: Nine independent solvent/temperature/time optimization entries were extracted row by row, including the 0% failure in entry 9 and all shared footnote quantities. Entry 1 was merged with its duplicate Scheme 2 (S,S) row.
Narrative comparison of optimization rows and selection of CH2Cl2 then 1,4-dioxane conditions; linked to the corresponding row records, with no extra experiment created.

Ten organohalide scope rows are shown. Table 2 entry 1 duplicates Table 1 entry 4 and was merged; entries 2-10 were extracted as nine distinct substrate-scope records with yield, dr, and product-specific ee values.
States high yield/enantioselectivity, retention of alkenyl-iodide C=C configuration for entries 7-9, and chemoselective C-I cleavage for 7e; linked to the relevant scope records.

unresolved: Table 1 entry 2 uses a mixed 0 °C-to-r.t. temperature program; r.t. was not converted to an assumed number.
The combined dr/ee cell for Table 1 entry 9 is printed as 0 at 0% yield, so no ratio or ee assignment was inferred.
Exact structural names/stereochemical SMILES for alkenyl iodides 7g-7i remain candidate interpretations of drawings.
Final product structures and yield measurement basis require source review; SI was not supplied.

regions.finding: States tentative configuration assignment for other products and that trans-pyrazolidine formation is favored; contextual evidence for the scope records, not a new experiment.
